prompt: Many believe that modern technology has brought people together, but others say that it has driven us apart. Discuss both viewpoints and give your own opinion.
essay:
A public discussion has emerged about whether technology has promoted unity among humans or resulted in increased isolation. I assert that the former is more accurate, although both sides have their advocates.

Certain opponents argue that technology has fostered a sense of alienation. They contend that while digital communication may be practical, it frequently fails to provide the emotional profundity of in-person interaction. Research has demonstrated that social media can induce isolation, as users frequently compare their lives to the idealised versions presented online. Furthermore, if smartphones had not become so widespread, people might have been more likely to focus on their real-world relationships. Conversely, it is undeniable that technology has revolutionised communication, creating new opportunities for collaboration, learning and bonding that were previously unimaginable. One argument in favour is that social media platforms and messaging apps allow people to create closeness, regardless of geographic barriers. Personally, I have formed friendships with individuals from different countries via online networks, enhancing cultural exchange, and I effortlessly maintain contact with my sister, who has moved overseas.

From my point of view, the impact of digital platforms on relationships depends largely on how they are used. Never has technology been so powerful in connecting individuals across the globe, and when employed mindfully, it can significantly strengthen relationships – especially professionally. For instance, tools such as Zoom and Google Meet allow specialists to share knowledge and support the community. Seldom do we acknowledge the role of innovations in medical research, where doctors consult international colleagues, or in education, where students gain access to world-class resources.

Thus, the advantages of modern technology in fostering unity and deepening expertise far outweigh the drawbacks of digital detachment.
